site_name: Microsoft San Antonio campus, Texas Research Park (Lambda Drive; SAT09-13, SAT40, SAT46)
notes: Our Pedernales Electric Coop assignment looks wrong. San Antonio Report (11 Dec 2023) describes the data centers 'proliferating on the city's far West Side' as CPS Energy customers that 'currently use about 324 megawatts' in aggregate, with CPS projecting roughly 2,700 MW more by end of 2028; a second San Antonio Report piece (1 Mar 2025, https://sanantonioreport.org/?p=5397838) says Microsoft has 'established a cluster of data centers on San Antonio's far West Side'. No retrieved source says in one sentence that CPS serves the Lambda Drive campus, hence medium, not high. Directory lead only (not cited): an on-site CPS 138 kV substation on a lot Microsoft deeded to the city in 2016. Tariff vs negotiated contract not established, so arrangement is unknown. Energized year not established: San Antonio Report (7 Aug 2023, https://sanantonioreport.org/microsoft-data-centers-san-antonio-region/) says Microsoft's first San Antonio-area centers of the last eight years were 'two centers built in 2015', and a May 2023 piece says it has built on Lambda Drive 'since 2016'; neither gives a first commercial-operation date for this campus, so our 2020 (from a 2019 generator permit) is probably a few years late but unverified. SAT40 (15000 Lambda Dr, $175.9M) was still under construction in Aug 2023. No public MW figure for the campus was found; the 324 MW is all far-west-side data centers on CPS in 2023, not Microsoft alone, so our 362.9 MW for this one campus is unverified and exceeds that 2023 aggregate. Research limit: the shared web-search budget (22 searches for this batch) was fully used; remaining nulls were not searched to exhaustion. Directory sites were used as leads only and are not cited.

site_name: Digital Realty Manassas, 9905 Godwin Dr (IAD53; 'Project Gold Manassas')
load_basis: Design critical capacity, not metered load: contractor award entry for Digital Realty 'Project Gold Manassas' describes a two-story, 185,211 sq ft, 36 MW data center with nine 2-MW generators. The entry gives no street address; it is matched to 9905 Godwin Dr by the 185,000 sq ft Digital Realty project reported for that address and the Godwin Drive duct-bank work it describes.
notes: Utility NOT established; three candidates remain. The contractor entry says the building 'would be the first data center built in the city of Manassas' and that utility power 'required a two-month road shutdown to get the electrical duct bank installed between existing utilities across Godwin Drive', without naming the utility. The City of Manassas runs its own electric utility and a city bid listing refers to a city substation on Godwin Drive; NOVEC is, as background not verified here, the co-op serving nearby Prince William County data center sites; and a directory listing (not cited) says Dominion. Our Dominion guess is therefore unverified and the city utility is a live alternative. Two searches found no city, commission or press source naming the provider; the Virginia DEQ permit document and the DCD and S&P articles could not be fetched (connection refused / 403). Year: the project was entered in the 2024 Excellence in Construction awards, so the building was complete by 2024, but the entry gives no completion date and 2023 vs 2024 cannot be told apart; left null (our 2024 is consistent). Load: 36 MW is well below our 85.7 MW. Caveat on the match: one report describes the 9905 Godwin building as single-story, the award entry as two-story. Digital Realty's other Manassas buildings (Brickyard Way, including the 96 MW 'Aurora' project announced Oct 2025) are separate and not counted here. Research limit: the shared web-search budget (22 searches for this batch) was fully used; remaining nulls were not searched to exhaustion. Directory sites were used as leads only and are not cited.

site_name: Amazon (AWS) Hermiston campus, NW Livestock Rd
notes: Our PacifiCorp assignment looks wrong. The Oregonian (M. Rogoway, carried by the La Grande Observer 11 Apr 2023) reports Amazon began working with Umatilla Electric Cooperative 'to choose the electricity supply for its huge data center operations near the communities of Boardman and Hermiston'; Data Center Frontier (14 Sep 2023, https://www.datacenterfrontier.com/energy/article/33011494/sabey-data-centers-plans-100-mw-multi-tenant-campus-in-gathering-eastern-oregon) says UEC 'serves AWS operations in Umatilla and Morrow Counties'. Neither names the Livestock Road parcel, hence medium. Arrangement is recorded as special_contract because of that reported supply-selection deal; its terms are not public. Open alternative to rule out: the City of Hermiston owns a municipal utility (Hermiston Energy Services; as background not verified here, it took over Pacific Power's Hermiston system, which may be why a PacifiCorp polygon covers this point), and an East Oregonian article (25 Apr 2024, https://eastoregonian.com/?p=651978) says Hermiston 'already has an enormous draw on the city's electrical grid' from the local data center and names Amazon. I am uncertain whether that refers to the municipal system or loosely to the area grid; if this parcel is on the municipal system the answer is Hermiston Energy Services, not UEC. BPA (our other candidate) is the wholesale supplier to both, not the retail provider. Year: no acceptable source; our 2019 rests on the 2018 generator permit, while a directory lead says the campus was first built in 2022. No public MW figure for this campus; CoBank (9 Jan 2026) shows UEC system load rising from about 300 MW in 2016 to about 1,400 MW in 2026, 80-85% data centers, which is system-wide. Research limit: the shared web-search budget (22 searches for this batch) was fully used; remaining nulls were not searched to exhaustion. Directory sites were used as leads only and are not cited.

serving_utility: Grant County PUD (PUD No. 2 of Grant County)
load_basis: UPPER BOUND, not metered load: nameplate of installed backup generators (21 x 2.25 MWe + 1 x 0.75 MWe = 48.0 MWe) listed in Ecology Approval Order 26AQ-E008 (22 Jan 2026), all installed Oct 2023-Jan 2024. Critical IT load is lower.
notes: Utility: Columbia Basin Herald (13 Feb 2023) on this project: 'The electricity is provided by the Grant County PUD and its hydropower projects.' No special contract found; recorded as retail. Year: our 2018 is wrong. The same article says site preparation began in late January 2023, and the paper wrote on 14 Oct 2023 that 'CyrusOne is building its first data facility in town'. Ecology's Jan 2026 order lists all 22 generators with install dates of Oct 2023 to Jan 2024 and calls the site an existing data center. First commercial operation is therefore 2024 at the earliest; 2024 is recorded at medium confidence, and 2025 cannot be excluded (a directory lead says 2025). The 2017-2019 permits were for a plan that was not built then. Load: the earlier permit (19AQ-E052, Oct 2019) covered 42 generators / about 91.5 MWe, which is what our 67.9 MW was derived from; the 2026 order cuts the facility total from 42 to 22 generators, so about 48 MWe of backup is what exists. If the pipeline scales generator nameplate to load, apply that scaling to 48, not 91.5. Planned buildout: the 2023 article says the site 'will be able to accommodate up to 90 megawatts'; the 2026 reduction to 22 generators suggests the near-term plan is smaller, so treat 90 as the original master plan. Research limit: the shared web-search budget (22 searches for this batch) was fully used; remaining nulls were not searched to exhaustion. Directory sites were used as leads only and are not cited.

site_name: NTT DATA Western Technology Center (former Dell data center), 525 D St NW, Quincy
serving_utility: Grant County PUD (PUD No. 2 of Grant County)
load_basis: UPPER BOUND, not metered load: nameplate of the five 3.0 MWe backup generators actually installed (15.0 MWe). Ecology Approval Order 11AQ-E421 Amended (4 May 2017) cut the permit from 28 generators / 84 MWe to these five because the later phases were never built. Critical IT load is lower.
notes: Utility: no source naming this customer was retrieved. Grant PUD states it serves 'customers throughout Grant County' and is the only mapped utility; Data Center Frontier (https://datacenterfrontier.com/hyperscale/article/33013783/vantage-data-centers-has-been-having-a-billion-dollar-moment-much-of-it-in-quincy-wa) lists NTT among the Quincy cluster and names Grant County PUD as the supplier for a neighbouring campus. That is stronger than a bare map inference (a county-wide public utility district with no competing retail provider) but is not a site-specific document, hence medium. Arrangement recorded as retail; no special contract found. Load: our 62.4 MW is overstated roughly fourfold. It derives from the original 2011 Dell permit for 28 generators (84 MWe) across three phases; Ecology's 2017 transfer order says 'only five (5) 3.0 MWe engine/generator sets have been installed to date' and limits the site to those five. Ecology's data center page (read 11 Nov 2026) shows no later permit for the site, so 15 MWe of backup is the current permitted total. If the pipeline scales generator nameplate to load, apply it to 15, not 84. Year: the five generators carry May 2011 build dates and the original order (5 Aug 2011) says Phase 1 construction 'will commence during 2011'; no source gives the first day of operation, so the year is left null (our 2012 is consistent with a directory lead). No planned-buildout figure is recorded because the unbuilt phases lapsed. Research limit: the shared web-search budget (22 searches for this batch) was fully used; remaining nulls were not searched to exhaustion. Directory sites were used as leads only and are not cited.
